## Motivation

Ported from the internal implementation.

Add CPU torch.compile graph support for both prefill and decode on Intel AMX systems, including static bucket graphs and optional dynamic-shape fallback graphs.

The implementation supports:

- Static prefill graphs using total-token buckets.
- Optional dynamic fallback graphs through `SGLANG_TORCH_DYNAMIC_SHAPE=true`.
- Exact buckets first, padded buckets second, and dynamic fallback last.

CPU prefill graphs are experimental and remain disabled by default; they must be explicitly enabled with the `full` backend.

## Modifications

- Extend `CPUGraphRunner` with CPU prefill graph capture and replay.
- Add static and dynamic graph support for both decode and prefill.
- Add prefill padding and hidden-state trimming.
- Define CPU decode configuration precedence:
  `decode.bs` > `decode.max_bs` > `--torch-compile-max-bs`.
- Generate prefill buckets from `prefill.max_bs` when needed.
- Reject unsupported CPU graph backends such as `breakable` and `tc_piecewise`.
- Add a stable prefill forward dispatcher to avoid unnecessary recompilation.
- Make layer-boundary objects compatible with TorchDynamo during CPU graph capture and replay.
- Fix graph breaks, runtime recompiles, and `InternalTorchDynamoError` failures related to `msgspec.Struct` objects and
  Python-side CPU capability checks.
- Update required CPU custom-op schemas, fake registrations, rotary embedding handling, and related kernels.
- Update CPU graph documentation and tests.

## Tests

- Cover backend gating, bucket generation, option precedence, padding, dispatcher stability, dynamic fallback, and encoder-decoder decode graph reuse.
- Reuse the existing real-model benchmark and MMLU test while enabling explicit CPU prefill graphs and dynamic-shape fallback.
- Verify graph and eager accuracy and graph execution without graph breaks or runtime recompiles.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Qwen3.5-35B (BF16, TP4) Prefill graph:  ~6% TTFT Speedup (BS=1, Input=1024).


## Checklist

- [ ] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [ ] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

## Review and Merge Process

1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process).
2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers.
3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so.
   - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci`
4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR.

+### CPU Graph for Decode and Prefill
+
+On Intel AMX systems, `torch.compile` can reduce Python overhead for CPU graph
+execution. Decode graph capture is enabled by default with
+`--enable-torch-compile`; CPU prefill graph capture is opt-in because the full
+prefill backend is experimental:
+
+```bash Command
+sglang serve \
+    --model-path <MODEL_ID_OR_PATH> \
+    --trust-remote-code \
+    --device cpu \
+    --attention-backend intel_amx \
+    --enable-torch-compile
+```
+
+`--enable-torch-compile` is the global compile switch. On CPU, decode defaults
+to `full`, while prefill defaults to `disabled`. CPU decode graphs use
+batch-size buckets; CPU prefill graphs use total-token buckets. To enable CPU
+prefill explicitly, set its backend to `full` in the shared JSON format:
+
+```bash Command
+sglang serve \
+    --model-path <MODEL_ID_OR_PATH> \
+    --trust-remote-code \
+    --device cpu \
+    --attention-backend intel_amx \
+    --enable-torch-compile \
+    --cuda-graph-config \
+    '{"decode":{"backend":"full", "max_bs": 4},"prefill":{"backend":"full", "max_bs": 512}}'
+```
+
+The JSON format works on CPU as well as CUDA. On CPU, the fields mean:
+
+- `decode.max_bs`: maximum decode batch size.
+- `decode.bs`: explicit decode batch-size buckets.
+- `prefill.max_bs`: maximum prefill total-token count.
+- `prefill.bs`: explicit prefill total-token buckets.
+
+For decode, `decode.bs` takes precedence over `decode.max_bs`; if both are
+omitted, the legacy `--torch-compile-max-bs` value is used. `decode.max_bs` or
+the legacy value then generates the default decode bucket list. For prefill,
+`prefill.bs` is generated from `prefill.max_bs` when it is omitted.
+
+To use custom buckets, set `bs` explicitly for each phase. In this example,
+decode captures batch sizes 1, 2, 4, and 8, while prefill captures total-token
+counts 128, 256, and 512:
+
+```bash Command
+sglang serve \
+    --model-path <MODEL_ID_OR_PATH> \
+    --trust-remote-code \
+    --device cpu \
+    --attention-backend intel_amx \
+    --enable-torch-compile \
+    --cuda-graph-config \
+    '{"decode":{"backend":"full", "bs": [1, 2, 4, 8]},"prefill":{"backend":"full", "bs": [128, 256, 512]}}'
+```
+
+When `bs` is provided, SGLang uses those buckets instead of generating them
+from `max_bs`.
+
+For workloads with batch sizes or prefill token counts that do not match the
+configured buckets, an optional dynamic fallback graph can be enabled with
+`SGLANG_TORCH_DYNAMIC_SHAPE=true`:
+
+```bash Command
+SGLANG_TORCH_DYNAMIC_SHAPE=true \
+sglang serve \
+    --model-path <MODEL_ID_OR_PATH> \
+    --trust-remote-code \
+    --device cpu \
+    --attention-backend intel_amx \
+    --enable-torch-compile
+```
+
+Dynamic graph compilation requires `--enable-torch-compile` and is available
+for both CPU decode and prefill. Exact configured buckets are used first;
+dynamic graphs are compiled as a fallback when no exact or padded bucket can
+serve the request. CPU prefill graphs currently target text-only requests;
+multimodal prefill requests fall back to eager execution. Dynamic graphs may
+increase startup compilation time.
+
+`full` is required in the JSON to enable CPU prefill. Set either phase to
+`disabled` to keep it on the eager path, for example:
+
+```bash Command
+--enable-torch-compile \
+--cuda-graph-config '{"decode":{"backend":"disabled"},"prefill":{"backend":"full"}}'
+```
+
+Unsupported phase backends such as `breakable` and `tc_piecewise` are rejected
+on CPU. Set a phase backend to `disabled` to keep that phase on the eager path.
+
+Legacy convenience parameters remain supported:
+
+- `--torch-compile-max-bs`: decode-only maximum batch size. It is used only
+    when explicit `decode.max_bs` and `decode.bs` are not provided.
+- `--cuda-graph-bs-decode`: explicit decode batch-size buckets.
+- `--cuda-graph-bs`: deprecated alias for `--cuda-graph-bs-decode`.
+- `--cuda-graph-max-bs-decode`: maximum decode batch size.
+- `--cuda-graph-max-bs`: deprecated alias for `--cuda-graph-max-bs-decode`.
+- `--cuda-graph-bs-prefill`: explicit prefill total-token buckets.
+- `--cuda-graph-max-bs-prefill`: maximum prefill total-token count on the CPU
+    graph path. The name is shared with other devices for compatibility.
+
 ## Benchmarking with Requests
 
 You can benchmark the performance via the `bench_serving` script.
